# About this qmd {.unnumbered}

Builds the prison exposure measures. Exposure is calculated for each
census tract first and then averaged up to the PUMA, so it reflects how
close prisons are to where people in the PUMA actually live. A prison
just across the PUMA boundary counts the same as one inside it.

The analysis qmd joins output if this qmd onto the 2022–2024 dataset.

Main measure, for tract $t$ and decay scale $h$ (km):

$$E_t(h) = \sum_{j} S_j \exp\left(-\frac{d_{tj}}{h}\right)$$

$d_{tj}$ is the distance from the tract to prison $j$. With $S_j = 1$, a
prison at distance 0 adds 1, a prison at distance $h$ adds 0.37, and one
at $3h$ adds 0.05. Small $h$ means only nearby prisons count; large $h$
means the regional concentration of prisons counts. I compute it for $h$
= 1, 5, 10, and 25, once with every prison counted equally ($S_j = 1$)
and once weighting prisons by capacity (in thousands of beds). h = 1 km
is the main measure.

The PUMA value is the average of its tracts, weighted by each tract's
non-institutional population (2020 census total minus people in
institutional group quarters), so incarcerated people don't give prison
tracts extra weight:

$$E_p = \frac{\sum_{t \in p} W_t E_t}{\sum_{t \in p} W_t}$$

Also built, as alternatives: whether there's a prison inside the PUMA
boundary, how many, and the distance from the average resident to the
nearest prison.

"Prisons" always means open state and federal facilities.

Outputs, in `data/final/`:

-   `tract_prison_exposure.csv`: exposure for every tract
-   `puma_prison_exposure.csv`: PUMA-level exposure, one row per PUMA.
    This is what `nationl_puma_analysis_2022_2024.qmd` reads.

# Setup

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(tigris)      
library(tidycensus)  

options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE)

state_fips <- unique(tidycensus::fips_codes$state_code)[1:51]   # 50 states + DC
h_values   <- c(1, 5, 10, 25)                                  # decay scales, km

```

# Prisons

```{r}
#| label: prisons
prisons_raw <- st_read("data/raw/prison-boundaries-1-geojson.geojson", quiet = TRUE) %>%
  st_make_valid()

# Open state and federal prisons, as points in a meters-based CRS (EPSG:5070).
# -999 is the source's missing-value code for capacity.
prisons <- prisons_raw %>%
  filter(STATUS == "OPEN", TYPE %in% c("STATE", "FEDERAL")) %>%
  mutate(CAPACITY = na_if(CAPACITY, -999)) %>%
  st_centroid() %>%
  st_transform(5070)

nrow(prisons)                         # should be 2005
table(prisons$TYPE)

# Is capacity reliable enough for the capacity-weighted measure? (No)
sum(is.na(prisons$CAPACITY))          # missing capacity
sum(prisons$CAPACITY <= 0, na.rm = TRUE)   # zero or negative 
summary(prisons$CAPACITY)
```

The capacity-weighted measure leaves out prisons with missing capacity.

# Tract locations and weights

Tract boundaries are downloaded once and saved as one point per tract.
`st_point_on_surface()` keeps the point inside the tract, which a
centroid doesn't always do for oddly shaped tracts.

```{r}
#| label: tract-points-download
#| eval: false

# One point per 2020 census tract, placed at the tract's center of population
# (Census Bureau, 2020 Centers of Population): the average location of where the
# tract's residents live, rather than the geometric middle of the tract.
# Not run when rendering; the saved file is read in the next chunk.
#read_csv("https://www2.census.gov/geo/docs/reference/cenpop2020/tract/CenPop2020_Mean_TR.txt",
#         col_types = cols(STATEFP = "c", COUNTYFP = "c", TRACTCE = "c")) %>%
#  mutate(GEOID = paste0(STATEFP, COUNTYFP, TRACTCE)) %>%
#  filter(STATEFP %in% state_fips) %>%                            # 50 states + DC
#  st_as_sf(coords = c("LONGITUDE", "LATITUDE"), crs = 4269) %>%  # Census coordinates (NAD83)
#  st_transform(5070) %>%                                         # same projection as before, distances in meters
#  select(GEOID) %>%
#  st_write("data/raw/tract_popcenters_2020.gpkg", delete_dsn = TRUE, quiet = TRUE)
```

```{r}
#| label: tract-points-load
tract_pts <- st_read("data/raw/tract_popcenters_2020.gpkg", quiet = TRUE)

nrow(tract_pts)   # ~84,000
```

```{r}
#| label: tract-weights
# GEOID is read as text so the leading zeros survive.
tract_pop_2020 <- read_csv("data/raw/tract_pop_2020.csv",
                           col_types = cols(GEOID = col_character()))

# Census tract -> 2020 PUMA relationship file.
rel20 <- read_csv("https://www2.census.gov/geo/docs/maps-data/data/rel2020/2020_Census_Tract_to_2020_PUMA.txt",
                  col_types = cols(.default = "c")) %>%
  transmute(GEOID   = paste0(STATEFP, COUNTYFP, TRACTCE),
            GEOID20 = paste0(STATEFP, PUMA5CE))

# Non-institutionalized population as the weight: total 2020 population minus people
# in institutional group quarters (prisons, nursing homes, etc.).
tract_weights <- tract_pop_2020 %>%
  mutate(pop_noninst = tot_pop - pop_inst_gq) %>%
  select(GEOID, tot_pop, pop_noninst, pop_correctional) %>%
  left_join(rel20, by = "GEOID")

# Checks
tract_pts %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  summarise(share_with_weight = mean(GEOID %in% tract_weights$GEOID))   # want ~1

tract_weights %>%
  select(pop_noninst) %>%
  summary()
```

# Tract-level exposure

Distances from every tract to every prison, including prisons in other
states. This is done one state at a time because the full 84,000 × 2,005
distance matrix doesn't fit in memory. It takes a few minutes the first
time; after that the saved file is read.

```{r}
#| label: tract-exposure-load
tract_exposure <- read_csv("data/final/tract_prison_exposure.csv",

nrow(tract_exposure)   # ~84,000

tract_exposure %>%
  select(starts_with("prison_exp_h")) %>%
```

# PUMA-level exposure

```{r}
#| label: puma-exposure
# Population-weighted average of tract exposure (weights: non-institutionalized population)
exposure_vars <- c("dist_nearest_prison_km",
                   paste0("prison_exp_h", h_values))

puma_exposure_decay <- tract_exposure %>%
  left_join(tract_weights, by = "GEOID") %>%
  filter(!is.na(GEOID20), pop_noninst > 0) %>%
  group_by(GEOID20) %>%
  summarise(
    across(c(dist_nearest_prison_km, starts_with("prison_exp"), starts_with("ring_")),
           ~ weighted.mean(.x, pop_noninst)),
    n_tracts_exposure = n()
  ) %>%
  rename(dist_nearest_prison_km_popw = dist_nearest_prison_km)   # distance for the average resident

# Presence and count inside the PUMA boundary (alternative measures)
# 2020 PUMA boundaries (cached by tigris after the first download)
pumas <- map_dfr(state_fips, ~ tigris::pumas(state = .x, cb = TRUE, year = 2020)) %>%
  select(GEOID20) %>%
  st_transform(5070)

prisons_in_puma <- st_join(prisons, pumas, join = st_within) %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  filter(!is.na(GEOID20)) %>%
  count(GEOID20, name = "num_prisons_in_puma")

puma_exposure <- pumas %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  left_join(puma_exposure_decay, by = "GEOID20") %>%
  left_join(prisons_in_puma, by = "GEOID20") %>%
  mutate(
    num_prisons_in_puma    = replace_na(num_prisons_in_puma, 0),
    prison_present_in_puma = as.integer(num_prisons_in_puma > 0)
  )

nrow(puma_exposure)                       # 2462
sum(is.na(puma_exposure$prison_exp_h25))  # ideally 0
write_csv(puma_exposure, "data/final/puma_prison_exposure.csv")
```

# Checks

```{r}
#| label: checks
# How the measures relate to each other: small h behaves like "is a prison nearby",
# large h like "regional concentration of prisons".
puma_exposure %>%
  select(prison_present_in_puma, num_prisons_in_puma, 
         starts_with("prison_exp_h")) %>%
  cor(use = "complete.obs", method = "spearman") %>%
  round(2)

# Distribution of the measure
summary(puma_exposure$prison_exp_h5)

# map of the h = 5 km measure
pumas %>%
  left_join(puma_exposure, by = "GEOID20") %>%
  filter(!substr(GEOID20, 1, 2) %in% c("02", "15")) %>%
  ggplot() +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = prison_exp_h5), colour = NA) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "Exposure\n(h = 5 km)", trans = "sqrt") +
  theme_void()
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-exposure-example
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 5.5

library(patchwork)

h_ex <- 5   # decay distance shown in the figure (km)

# Example PUMA: one that contains exactly one prison (change to any GEOID20 you like)
puma_exp <- read_csv("data/final/puma_prison_exposure.csv",
                     col_types = cols(GEOID20 = col_character()))

example_puma <- puma_exp %>%
  filter(num_prisons_in_puma == 1) %>%
  slice_max(prison_exp_h5, n = 1) %>%
  pull(GEOID20)

# PUMA outline and its tracts (polygons only for the picture)
puma_shape <- st_read("data/final/national_puma_dataset_2022_2024.gpkg", quiet = TRUE) %>%
  filter(GEOID20 == example_puma) %>%
  st_transform(5070)

ex_tracts <- tract_weights %>%
  filter(GEOID20 == example_puma) %>%
  left_join(tract_exposure %>% select(GEOID, prison_exp_h5), by = "GEOID")

tract_shapes <- tigris::tracts(state = str_sub(example_puma, 1, 2), cb = TRUE, year = 2020) %>%
  filter(GEOID %in% ex_tracts$GEOID) %>%
  st_transform(5070) %>%
  left_join(ex_tracts, by = "GEOID")

ex_centers <- tract_pts %>% filter(GEOID %in% ex_tracts$GEOID)

# Example tract: the one with the highest exposure in this PUMA
ex_tract_id <- ex_tracts %>% slice_max(prison_exp_h5, n = 1) %>% pull(GEOID)
ex_pt <- ex_centers %>% filter(GEOID == ex_tract_id)

# Rings at h, 2h and 3h around the example tract's population center
rings <- tibble(k = 1:3, label = c("h", "2h", "3h")) %>%
  mutate(geometry = map(k, ~ st_geometry(st_buffer(ex_pt, .x * h_ex * 1000))[[1]])) %>%
  st_as_sf(crs = 5070)

# Prisons within 3h, with their distance and weight
near_prisons <- prisons %>%
  mutate(d_km = as.numeric(st_distance(geometry, ex_pt)) / 1000) %>%
  filter(d_km <= 3 * h_ex) %>%
  mutate(weight = exp(-d_km / h_ex),
         label  = sprintf("%.1f km → %.2f", d_km, weight))

tract_value <- ex_tracts %>% filter(GEOID == ex_tract_id) %>% pull(prison_exp_h5)
puma_value  <- puma_exp %>% filter(GEOID20 == example_puma) %>% pull(prison_exp_h5)

# Panel A: the map
map_box <- st_bbox(st_union(st_geometry(puma_shape), st_geometry(rings)))

p_map <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = tract_shapes, aes(fill = prison_exp_h5), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_sf(data = puma_shape, fill = NA, colour = "grey20", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_sf(data = rings, fill = NA, colour = "grey40", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_sf_text(data = rings %>% st_cast("LINESTRING") %>% st_line_sample(sample = 0.25) %>%
                 st_as_sf() %>% mutate(label = rings$label),
               aes(label = label), size = 3, colour = "grey30", nudge_y = 600) +
  geom_sf(data = ex_centers, colour = "grey45", size = 0.8) +
  geom_sf(data = ex_pt, colour = "black", size = 2.5) +
  geom_sf(data = near_prisons, shape = 17, colour = "#B23A1E", size = 3) +
  geom_sf_label(data = near_prisons, aes(label = label), size = 2.8,
                nudge_y = 1500, label.size = 0, alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Greys", direction = 1,
                       name = paste0("Tract exposure\n(h = ", h_ex, " km)")) +
  coord_sf(xlim = map_box[c("xmin", "xmax")], ylim = map_box[c("ymin", "ymax")]) +
  labs(title = "A. One PUMA, its tracts and nearby prisons") +
  theme_void() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

# Panel B: how much a prison counts, by distance
decay <- expand_grid(h = c(1, 5, 10, 25), d_km = seq(0, 40, by = 0.25)) %>%
  mutate(weight = exp(-d_km / h),
         main   = h == h_ex)

p_curve <- ggplot(decay, aes(d_km, weight, group = h)) +
  geom_line(data = filter(decay, !main), colour = "grey70", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_line(data = filter(decay, main), colour = "black", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_text(data = decay %>% group_by(h) %>% filter(d_km == 6),
            aes(label = paste0("h = ", h)), hjust = 0, nudge_y = 0.03, size = 3,
            colour = "grey30") +
  geom_point(data = st_drop_geometry(near_prisons), aes(d_km, weight), inherit.aes = FALSE,
             shape = 17, colour = "#B23A1E", size = 3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = exp(-1), linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey50") +
  annotate("text", x = 40, y = exp(-1), label = "0.37 at d = h", hjust = 1, vjust = -0.5,
           size = 3, colour = "grey40") +
  labs(title = "B. How much one prison counts",
       x = "Distance from tract population center (km)",
       y = "Contribution of one prison, exp(−d / h)") +
  theme_minimal()

p_map + p_curve +
  plot_layout(widths = c(1.3, 1)) +
  plot_annotation(
    caption = sprintf(paste(
      "Example tract (black dot): exposure = sum of prison contributions = %.2f (h = %d km).",
      "Prisons farther than 3h add less than 0.05 each but are still counted.",
      "PUMA value = population-weighted average of its tracts = %.2f.", sep = "\n"),
      tract_value, h_ex, puma_value),
    theme = theme(plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0)))
```

```{r}
#| label: exposure-example-candidates

puma_exp <- read_csv("data/final/puma_prison_exposure.csv",
                     col_types = cols(GEOID20 = col_character()))

puma_info <- st_read("data/final/national_puma_dataset_2022_2024.gpkg", quiet = TRUE) %>%
  st_transform(5070) %>%
  select(GEOID20, NAMELSAD20, STUSPS20)

# PUMAs with exactly one prison, most locally exposed first
puma_exp %>%
  filter(num_prisons_in_puma >= 1) %>%
  left_join(st_drop_geometry(st_read("data/final/national_puma_dataset_2022_2024.gpkg", quiet = TRUE)) %>%
              select(GEOID20, NAMELSAD20, STUSPS20, pct_pop_nonmetro),
            by = "GEOID20") %>%
  filter(pct_pop_nonmetro > 50) %>%
  arrange(desc(prison_exp_h1)) %>%
  select(GEOID20, NAMELSAD20, STUSPS20, num_prisons_in_puma, prison_exp_h1, prison_exp_h5) %>%
  head(15)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-exposure-example
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 6

library(patchwork)

h_ex         <- 5               # decay distance shown (km): 1, 5, 10 or 25
example_puma <- "3600704"       # Cayuga & Onondaga (South) Counties PUMA, NY
example_tract <- "36011042100"  # Census Tract 421, next to Auburn Correctional Facility

exp_col <- paste0("prison_exp_h", h_ex)   # exposure column that matches h_ex

puma_shape <- puma_info %>% filter(GEOID20 == example_puma)

# Tracts in the PUMA, with their exposure (for h_ex) and weights
ex_tracts <- tract_weights %>%
  filter(GEOID20 == example_puma) %>%
  left_join(tract_exposure %>% select(GEOID, exposure = all_of(exp_col)), by = "GEOID")

# All tracts in the state (neighbors are drawn in grey), and this PUMA's tracts
state_tracts <- tigris::tracts(state = str_sub(example_puma, 1, 2), cb = TRUE, year = 2020) %>%
  st_transform(5070)

tract_shapes <- state_tracts %>%
  filter(GEOID %in% ex_tracts$GEOID) %>%
  left_join(ex_tracts, by = "GEOID")

ex_centers <- tract_pts %>% filter(GEOID %in% ex_tracts$GEOID)

# Example tract
ex_tract <- tract_shapes %>% filter(GEOID == example_tract)
ex_pt    <- ex_centers %>% filter(GEOID == example_tract)
ex_xy    <- st_coordinates(ex_pt)

# Rings at h, 2h, 3h around the example tract's population center
rings <- tibble(k = 1:3) %>%
  mutate(geometry = map(k, ~ st_geometry(st_buffer(ex_pt, .x * h_ex * 1000))[[1]])) %>%
  st_as_sf(crs = 5070)

# Ring labels on each circle, at the chosen angle
angle <- 180 * pi / 180   # 0 = right, 90 = top, 180 = left, 270 = bottom
ring_labels <- tibble(k = 1:3,
                      x = ex_xy[, "X"] + cos(angle) * (1:3) * h_ex * 1000,
                      y = ex_xy[, "Y"] + sin(angle) * (1:3) * h_ex * 1000,
                      label = paste0(c("h", "2h", "3h"), " = ", (1:3) * h_ex, " km"))

# Prisons within 4h, with their distance and weight
near_prisons <- prisons %>%
  mutate(d_km = as.numeric(st_distance(geometry, ex_pt)) / 1000) %>%
  filter(d_km <= 4 * h_ex) %>%
  mutate(weight = exp(-d_km / h_ex),
         label  = sprintf("%s\n%.2f km → %.2f", str_to_title(NAME), d_km, weight))

tract_value <- ex_tract$exposure
puma_value  <- puma_exp %>% filter(GEOID20 == example_puma) %>% pull(all_of(exp_col))

# Map window: 4h around the example tract
zoom <- 3.3 * h_ex * 1000

# Legend entries
ex_label     <- paste0("Population center of ", ex_tract$NAMELSAD)
point_breaks <- c(ex_label, "Population centers of other tracts", "State or federal prison")
line_breaks  <- c("PUMA boundary",
                  paste0("Distance rings (", h_ex, ", ", 2 * h_ex, ", ", 3 * h_ex, " km)"))

# Panel A: map
p_map <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = state_tracts, fill = "grey94", colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_sf(data = tract_shapes, aes(fill = exposure), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_sf(data = puma_shape, aes(linetype = line_breaks[1]), fill = NA,
          colour = "grey15", linewidth = 0.8, key_glyph = "path") +
  geom_sf(data = rings, aes(linetype = line_breaks[2]), fill = NA,
          colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.5, key_glyph = "path") +
  geom_label(data = ring_labels, aes(x, y, label = label), size = 2.8,
             fill = "white", label.size = 0, label.padding = unit(0.1, "lines")) +
  geom_sf(data = ex_centers, aes(colour = point_breaks[2]), size = 1) +
  geom_sf(data = near_prisons, aes(colour = point_breaks[3]), shape = 17, size = 3.5) +
  ggrepel::geom_label_repel(
    data = near_prisons,
    aes(label = label, geometry = geometry),
    stat = "sf_coordinates",
    size = 2.8, fill = "white", colour = "black",
    label.size = 0.2, lineheight = 0.9,
    box.padding = 0.8, min.segment.length = 0,
    seed = 1
  ) +
  geom_sf(data = ex_pt, aes(colour = point_breaks[1]), size = 3.5,
          shape = 21, fill = "black", stroke = 1.2) +       # drawn last, on top
  scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Blues", direction = 1,
                       name = paste0("Tract exposure (h = ", h_ex, " km)"),
                       guide = guide_colourbar(order = 1, title.position = "top",
                                               barwidth = unit(4, "cm"))) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    name = NULL,
    breaks = point_breaks,
    values = setNames(c("white", "grey40", "#B23A1E"), point_breaks),
    guide = guide_legend(order = 2, ncol = 1,
                         override.aes = list(shape = c(21, 19, 17), size = c(3.5, 1.5, 3.5),
                                             fill = c("black", NA, NA),
                                             colour = c("black", "grey40", "#B23A1E")))
  ) +
  scale_linetype_manual(
    name = NULL,
    breaks = line_breaks,
    values = setNames(c("solid", "dashed"), line_breaks),
    guide = guide_legend(order = 3, ncol = 1,
                         override.aes = list(colour = c("grey15", "grey30"),
                                             linewidth = c(0.8, 0.5)))
  ) +
  coord_sf(xlim = ex_xy[, "X"] + c(-zoom, zoom),
           ylim = ex_xy[, "Y"] + c(-zoom, zoom), expand = FALSE) +
  labs(title    = paste0("A. ", puma_shape$NAMELSAD20, ", ", puma_shape$STUSPS20),
       subtitle = paste0(ex_tract$NAMELSAD, ", ", ex_tract$NAMELSADCO,
                         " (GEOID ", ex_tract$GEOID, ")")) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        plot.title.position = "plot",
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, colour = "grey30"))

# Panel B: how much one prison counts, by distance
decay <- expand_grid(h = c(1, 5, 10, 25), d_km = seq(0, 30, by = 0.1)) %>%
  mutate(weight = exp(-d_km / h))

p_curve <- ggplot(decay, aes(d_km, weight, group = h)) +
  geom_line(data = filter(decay, h != h_ex), colour = "grey75", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_line(data = filter(decay, h == h_ex), colour = "black", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_text(data = decay %>% filter(abs(d_km - 4) < 0.05),
            aes(label = paste0("h = ", h)), hjust = 0, nudge_x = 0.3, size = 3,
            colour = "grey30") +
  geom_point(data = st_drop_geometry(near_prisons), aes(d_km, weight), inherit.aes = FALSE,
             shape = 17, colour = "#B23A1E", size = 3.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = exp(-1), linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey50") +
  annotate("text", x = 30, y = exp(-1), label = "0.37 at d = h", hjust = 1, vjust = -0.5,
           size = 3, colour = "grey40") +
  labs(title = "B. How much one prison counts",
       x = "Distance from tract population center (km)",
       y = "Contribution of one prison, exp(−d / h)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

# Combine: legends collected below both panels
p_map + p_curve +
  plot_layout(widths = c(1.2, 1), guides = "collect") +
  plot_annotation(
    caption = sprintf(paste(
      "%s: exposure = sum of all prison contributions = %.2f (h = %d km).",
      "PUMA value = average of its tracts, weighted by non-institutional population = %.2f.",
      sep = "\n"),
      ex_tract$NAMELSAD, tract_value, h_ex, puma_value),
    theme = theme(plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 9))) &
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.box = "horizontal",
        legend.justification = "left",
        legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
        legend.title = element_text(size = 8))
```

# Variables added {.unnumbered}

| Variable | Meaning |
|----|----|
| `prison_exp_h1`, `_h5`, `_h10`, `_h25`, `_h50`, `_h100` | distance-decay exposure, every prison counts equally (h = 25 is the main measure) |
| `prison_exp_cap_h1` … `_h100` | same, prisons weighted by capacity in thousands of beds; prisons with unknown capacity left out |
| `num_prisons_in_puma`, `prison_present_in_puma` | prisons inside the PUMA boundary; any (0/1) |
| `n_tracts_exposure` | number of tracts averaged |
